about.title: Maywood Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Maywood is a small, tightly packed city, but its traffic corridors carry a steady flow of cars every day. Public records show 63 injury collisions and 79 injured people in the most recent reporting year, with crashes clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. — a pattern that likely reflects the end-of-week rush along Slauson Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, Pine Avenue, and 59th Place. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories fade quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney working in Los Angeles County who can review your crash, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid common missteps like giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before you understand your rights.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government vehicle or road defect was involved — relevant given Maywood's city-maintained corridors. An attorney can flag deadlines early so you don't lose your claim before it starts.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault just reduces the award. An independent attorney can help make sure the insurer doesn't unfairly inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages, But Insurers Will Push Back Anyway
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, yet adjusters often lowball these claims hoping you don't know that. Having someone in your corner who understands how to document and present these losses can make a real difference.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can talk to the insurer on your behalf so you don't have to navigate that alone.

items.question: What if my accident happened at one of Maywood's busier intersections, like near Slauson Avenue or Atlantic Boulevard?
items.answer: Crashes on higher-volume corridors like these often involve more parties, more insurance companies, and more disputed facts about who had the right of way. An attorney can help gather traffic camera footage, city records, and witness statements before that evidence disappears. This is especially important if a city vehicle or roadway condition was involved, since claims against government entities have shorter deadlines.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency — meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
